sections.h2: Hazard offices for Perry County property tax
sections.html:
Everything a seller needs is in Hazard. Upstairs in the courthouse at 481 Main Street, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) appraises property, and the County Clerk has the ground-floor counter. Bills are mailed and collected by the Sheriff's Office on East Main Street.

  • Sheriff's tax office: 124 East Main Street; letters go to box 7309, Hazard 41702. Hours are 8:00 to 4:00 on weekdays, minus holidays. The number is 606-439-4523, option 2.
  • PVA: 606-436-4914. The sheriff's tax page links to the parcel search the PVA maintains.
  • County Clerk: 606-436-4614.

Checks to the sheriff are made payable to "Perry County Sheriff." A separate billing provider handles online payment and adds its own convenience fee.

The statewide schedule applies in Perry County under KRS 134.015.

The mailing date changes yearly, so the tax office at 606-439-4523 is the place to confirm what is printed on a given bill. The sheriff collects state, county and district taxes and is paid a commission on what it collects. Late-starting years follow a slower pattern in which each stage lasts a full month.

The sheriff's tax office at 124 East Main Street takes payments Monday through Friday from 8:00 to 4:00, except on holidays. By mail, write the check to "Perry County Sheriff" and send it to box 7309, Hazard 41702. Online payment goes through a separate billing provider that charges its own convenience fee, so a check or a counter payment costs less. If something about the bill looks wrong, call 606-439-4523 and press option 2 before you pay, and ask the PVA at 606-436-4914 about any question of value.

Keep the receipt. A buyer's title company will ask for proof that the year's bill is paid or a figure to prorate at closing.

Delinquency costs more each month it continues. Bills not paid by April 15 go to the County Clerk, where interest of one percent a month, clerk commissions and attorney commissions pile up. The clerk's sale comes 90 to 135 days after the transfer.

The County Clerk's website points to a delinquent tax application, and the county attorney's office can set up an installment plan on a current delinquency. If you are selling, ask for a payoff in writing, because the balance changes every month the bill stays open.

sections.h2: Can a Perry County owner contest the value?
sections.html: Yes, and the route starts at the PVA's office, where the owner sits down with staff before anything is filed. The written appeal then goes to the clerk's desk by the end of the day after the thirteen-day roll inspection closes. A panel of neighbors on the local board decides, usually within five weeks, and it looks for hard evidence such as appraisals, repair bids and nearby sales.

A homeowner who is 65 or older, or who is classed as totally disabled, can claim $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026.

Bring a birth certificate, license or other proof of age when you apply, and file before the roll closes for the year so the deduction shows on your bill.

sections.h2: What a seller pays to record a deed
sections.html:
The grantor owes Kentucky's transfer tax, a half dollar for every $500 of price in the deed, counting a partial $500 as whole (KRS 142.050), and the clerk takes it before accepting the instrument. The Perry County Clerk's published minimums are $50 for a deed and $80 for a mortgage, and a deed adds $3 for each page after the fifth.

A title company will expect the current tax bill to be paid or prorated, a clerk's payoff if an earlier year went delinquent, and an in-care-of address on the deed for the next bill. The clerk's office can quote the total for any document, and staff there cannot run a title search, so an attorney or abstractor handles that step. The clerk's office also offers a free DocAlert service that emails owners when a deed or mortgage is filed in their name.

Prices here are low. Median owner-occupied value is $91,800, and 70.4% of homes are owner-occupied. Household income is $42,181 at the midpoint.

  • Estimated 2025 population is 26,555, down 6.7% from 28,473 in the 2020 count.
  • Rent has a median of $798. Owner costs run $1,167 with a mortgage and $379 without one.
  • In 2020 the county had 13,213 housing units, 13.1% of them vacant. The 2025 estimate is 13,425 units, with zero building permits issued.

With a falling population and many empty units, price carefully and be ready to show the condition of the house.

sections.h2: Setting and taxes for business sellers
sections.html:
Perry County covers about 343 square miles of the Appalachian coalfield. Hazard and Buckhorn are the two incorporated cities. Homes are served by two school systems, Perry County Schools and Hazard Independent Schools, so buyers often ask which one covers an address.

Business owners should note that Perry County is a stacked occupational license county. The tax is 1% of wages and net profit, and anyone working inside Hazard city limits pays both the county and the city. A seller of a rental or a commercial building should raise this with an accountant before closing.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed, step by step
sections.html:
If a year is delinquent, the sale can still go forward. The key is to know the exact number and to clear it at closing.

  1. Find out where the bill sits. Before April 15 it is with the sheriff, and after that date it is with the County Clerk.
  2. Ask for a written payoff, since interest and commissions change monthly.
  3. If the debt is large, call the county attorney's office about an installment plan on a current delinquency.
  4. Give the payoff to the title company so it is paid from your proceeds.
  5. Confirm that a release is recorded and keep a copy.

Selling for cash can shorten the wait for a buyer's loan and appraisal, but the tax debt still has to be paid at the table. Handle it early, and the rest of the sale is simpler.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Perry County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Sheriff's Office, 124 East Main Street, Hazard, on weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00. Payments by post use box 7309, with checks written to Perry County Sheriff.

faqs.q: How much does the homestead exemption take off a Perry County home?
faqs.a: The deduction is $49,100 against assessed value for 2025 and 2026, for owners 65 or older or totally disabled. The PVA has the form.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a Perry County sale?
faqs.a: The rate is a half dollar for every $500 of the price stated in the deed, and the seller pays it. The clerk collects it before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Where do unpaid Perry County bills go after April 15?
faqs.a: They move to the county clerk as certificates of delinquency, with interest at one percent a month plus clerk and attorney fees.

faqs.q: Who decides a Perry County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: A local board of area property owners. The owner must meet the PVA first and file with the clerk by the workday after roll inspection closes.
